pr_title: pm: policy: low latency events handling
pr_body:
Some events needs to be handled with a very low latency constraint. If the system is in deep sleep, exit latency from this low level state exceeds sometimes the maximum latency constraint of these events.

Before suspending the system, select which events is happening sooner, kernel events or normal events.
CPU will be up just before the next event occurs taking into account the exit latency of the current power state

Change also the policy event API to take as argument absolute time in HW cycles instead of time in us

Fixes #64753

issue_context.title: PM policy: register events requiring low handling latency
issue_context.body:
**The problem**

Embedded programs often wait for an event. Some events have predictable timing: e.g. the next scheduled timer event, the end of an ongoing SPI transaction. Some of these events must be handled with low latency to meet specification requirements (e.g. send ACK within a limited time window).

Currently, Zephyr PM policy exposes API to register expected events: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/8bcdb694a23a23d2f93bea4dc3d02136e14576df/include/zephyr/pm/policy.h#L201
However, the information provided for this function is used only to calculate expected residency when the idle thread selects the next sleep state. The problem is that the registered event is handled with the latency introduced by exiting the selected sleep state, which can be longer than acceptable.

**The desired solution**

I would like to extend the `pm_policy_event_register()` with a new parameter: `bool low_latency`.

When the idle thread prepares to enter sleep and during residency calculation it finds out that the next expected event is a registered one with `low_latency` set to `true`, it must run a procedure similar to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e07ded1656b49a75699ad881004d48c23c42c7a8/subsys/pm/pm.c#L202 to prepare system wake-up in advance of the expected event, so that at the time the event arrives the system is active and can handle the event without latency.

**The considered alternatives**

An alternative would be to use the existing function: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/8bcdb694a23a23d2f93bea4dc3d02136e14576df/include/zephyr/pm/policy.h#L148. However this function would prevent entering sleep states while waiting for an event. So if the event is expected in 3 seconds, the system would remain active (or in light sleep) for 3 seconds, instead of more efficiently entering deep sleep and scheduling a wake-up in 2.9 s.

Another alternative would be to extend the `pm_policy_event_register()` with the `int max_acceptable_latency_in_us` parameter, but the exact calculations of acceptable latency and wake-up time management seem like an overkill.

Another option is to set a `k_timer` a little ahead of the event by the module registering the event. However, there are a few drawbacks to this pattern:
1. The module registering the event does not know which sleep state will be entered just before the event, so it does not know the exit latency and it would need to always prepare for the max possible wake-up latency, often waking up the system too early.
2. If multiple modules register events to be handled with low latency, they would need to repeat similar code instead of reusing one created in the power management subsystem.
